newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam set for 8.3 mln tonnes crude output in '96.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam set for 8.3 mln tonnes crude output in '96.

text.p: Vietnam's crude oil production is expected to rise to 8.3 million tonnes this year from 7.7 million in 1995, the state-run Saigon Times Daily said in a report quoting Petrovietnam Director General Ho Si Thoang.

The state oil and gas firm chief said that at least three new offshore fields would be go into operation by 1998 as part of a drive to lift output to between 18 and 20 million tonnes a year by the end of the century.

He told the paper that the PM-3 field, in an overlapping area jointly developed by Petrovietnam and Malaysia's national oil company Petronas, would start production early next year. PM-3 would also produce commercial natural gas by 1999, he added. The other two fields due to start up by 1998 were Hong Ngoc (Ruby) and Rang Dong, which will be exploited by Petronas and Mitsubishi Oil respectively.
Thoang said initial data showed that reserves at Rang Dong were bigger than those at Hong Ngoc.

He added that the two gas fields of Lan Tay and Lan Do, being developed by an alliance between British Petroleum Co Plc and Norway's Statoil, would also go into operation in 1998. Reserves of natural gas at the two fields has been estimated at 60 billion cubic metres.
